title: Balanced K-flat model for a derived tensor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ and $R'$ be commutative $R$-algebras, and let $M$ be a complex of $A$-modules, viewed on the one-point ringed site and in the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $P\to M$ is a K-flat resolution in $A$-modules and $F\to R'$ is a K-flat resolution in $R$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], then the total complex $P\otimes_R F$ represents $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$ in the derived category of $A$-modules. Multiplication by elements of $R'$ gives commuting endomorphisms in that derived category and hence an $A\otimes_R R'$-module structure on cohomology. The construction is independent of the chosen resolutions up to the canonical isomorphism in the derived category and is functorial in $M$.

source.place: Tags 064K and 06Y6 (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism, lemma-derived-base-change), balanced derived tensor via K-flat resolutions

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] to R to A. Its functor U on A-complexes inverts quasi-isomorphisms by its last clause. Use Localization.lift along Q_A and Localization.fac to obtain the bifunctor T on D(A). The signed mapBifunctorFlipIso of Mathlib identifies its opposite-order totalization with the mixedTotalTensor of [def-pc-mixed-total-tensor]; transport the counit through this isomorphism and the localization comparison. IsRightKanExtension transport proves the left-derived universal property, and the K-flat counit clause gives computation on F. Naturality follows by composing the localization, counit, and signed flip naturality equations.

For q:P to M and f:F to R′[0], Q_A(q) and Q_R(f) are isomorphisms. The counit at F is invertible by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. Define e as the inverse of that counit followed by T(Q_A(q)) at Q_R(F), then T(Q_A(M))(Q_R(f)). Its compatibility equation follows from inverse cancellation; uniqueness follows by cancelling the counit and Iso.ext. This uses no extra K-flatness of P over R, nor any new choice of P; the hypothesis that P is K-flat over A is retained.

The pointwise derived functor is additive because the triangulated structure in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] gives additivity; transport it across the localization comparison. Construct multiplication as a ring map from R′ to End of R′ as an R-module, and compose the additive single, localization, and derived functors. This gives rho with the required formula. Naturality of the first-variable transformation evaluated at multiplication by b gives its commutation with multiplication by a.

Prove common-R scalar compatibility in three local helpers. On each total-tensor summand extension of scalars sends r times identity to algebraMap(R,A)(r) times identity, by the pure tensor balancing relation; tensorLeft linearity and total-summand extensionality give the complex identity. Homology naturality and ShortComplex.homologyMap_smul give the same identity for H(Q(K)). For the derived functor use the actual source-library functorial flat resolution (ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution, Abelian.LeftResolution.reduced and kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj), with K-flatness in the ordinary-module predicate [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. The invertible counit on a K-flat model and its naturality transfer the scalar identity to that model; naturality of the resolution map and cancellation of its derived homology image transfer it to every complex. Compose rho with homology and ModuleCat.endRingEquiv. The resulting R′ ring map to A-linear endomorphisms agrees with A-scalars on R. Make it an R-algebra map, pair it with the central A-scalar algebra map, and apply Algebra.TensorProduct.lift. Restriction of the evaluation module along this ring map constructs the required module on the original cohomology carrier; lift_tmul gives the exact pure-tensor action equation.
